title: नेवाः संस्कारमा चित्रकलाको प्रयोग
nepali: नेपालमण्डलका बासिन्दा नेवारहरुले जीवनलाई आलंकारिक बनाउन जीवनमा अपनाउँदै आइरहेको हरेक संस्कृति र संस्कारका कर्महरुमा मूर्तिकला, वास्तुकला, संगितकला, चित्रकलाको प्रयोग भइरहेको छ। चित्रकला सौन्दर्यको प्रतीक मात्र नभै मानवको अन्तरहृदयको भाव पोख्ने माध्यम पनि हो । त्यसैले कलाको माध्यमबाट मानव सभ्यताको पहिचान हुन्छ । कलाको माध्यमबाट संस्कृतिको जन्म हुन्छ । संस्कृतिले कलालाई जीवन्त बनाउँछ । कला र संस्कृति शरीर र प्राण जस्तै अन्योन्याश्रित सम्बन्ध छ । संस्कृतिको विस्तृत रुप संस्कार हो । यस लेखमा नेवारहरुले जन्मदेखि मृत्युसम्मका संस्कार कर्महरुमा के कस्ता चित्रहरु प्रयोग गरेका छन् ? ती चित्रहरु किन कुन दर्शनबाट प्रभावित भएर प्रयोग गरेका हुन् ? संस्कारमा चित्रकला किन प्रयोग गरिन्छ ? भन्ने प्रश्नको उत्तर खोज्नु यो लेखको उद्देश्य हो । यसको लागि समाजशास्त्र सिद्धान्त अपनाई ब्याख्या विश्लेषण गरिने छ । यो अनुसन्धान स्रोतको रुपमा मुख्य रुपमा पुस्तकहरुको अध्ययन भएको छ । यस अनुसन्धानात्मक लेखको लेखक स्वयं वज्रयानी समाजमा रही संस्कार कर्मको अवलोकन, सहभागी गर्दै आइरहेको हुनाले अनुभव र अवलोकन गरिएका अनुभव र त्यस्तो संस्कारसंग सम्बन्धित फोटोहरु समावेश गरिएको छ । नेवार संस्कारमा विविध कलाको प्रयोग हुने भए तापनि यसमा विशेष गरी नेवारहरुको जीवनमा गरिने संस्कारमा चित्रकलाको प्रयोगलाई केन्द्र बनाई अध्ययन गरिएको छ ।
american_english: In every cultural and ritual practice that the Newars, the residents of Nepal Mandala, have been adopting in life to make life ornamental, sculpture, architecture, music, and painting are being used. Painting is not only a symbol of beauty, but also a medium for expressing the inner feelings of human beings. Therefore, human civilization is identified through the medium of art. Through the medium of art, culture is born. Culture makes art vibrant. Art and culture share an interdependent relationship, just like body and life-breath. Ritual is the elaborate form of culture. In this article, seeking answers to the questions—what kinds of paintings have Newars used in ritual practices from birth to death? Why and influenced by which philosophy were those paintings used? Why is painting used in rituals?—is the objective of this article. For this, adopting sociological theory, explanation and analysis will be carried out. As the source of this research, primarily the study of books has been conducted. Since the author of this research article has himself been living in Vajrayana society, observing and participating in ritual practices, personal experiences, observed experiences, and photographs related to such rituals have been included. Although diverse arts are used in Newar rituals, in this study, the use of painting in rituals performed throughout the life of Newars has specifically been made the central focus of the study.

informal_english: In every cultural and ritual act that the Newars living in Nepal Mandala have been adopting in life to make life decorative, sculpture, architecture, music, and painting are being used. Painting is not just a symbol of beauty, but also a medium to pour out the innermost feelings of the human heart. That is why human civilization gets identified through the medium of art. Through the medium of art, culture is born. Culture makes art truly vibrant. Art and culture have an interdependent bond, just like body and prana. Samskara is basically the elaborate form of culture. In this article, the main objective is to find answers to the questions: what kinds of paintings have Newars used in rituals from birth to death? Why and influenced by which philosophy were those paintings used? Why is painting used in rituals at all? For this, sociological theory will be adopted to carry out the explanation and analysis. As the main research source, primarily the study of books has been done. Since the author of this research article has himself been staying in the Vajrayani community, observing and participating in ritual practices, personal experiences, observed experiences, and photos related to such rituals have been included. Although diverse arts are used in Newar rituals, here the use of painting in rituals performed in the life of Newars has specifically been made the central focus of study.
translator_notes: The abstract features embedded rhetorical questions within a single sentence, which have been preserved in order. Sociological and cultural terms such as Nepal Mandala (नेपालमण्डल), Newar (नेवार), Vajrayana (वज्रयान), and Samskara (संस्कार) are transliterated. Strict clause and sentence order maintained.
